title: PIR: Improving Time Series Forecasting via Instance-aware Post-hoc Revision

split.decision: ETTh1 official chronological split: train [0,8640), val [8640,11520), test [11520,14400); each forecast has 96 previous rows. Every 8th window evaluated, out of 2785/2689/2545/2161 per split/horizon (drop_last=False). No randomized split. Training and retrieval use train only; early stopping uses original shuffled validation loader.

baseline.paper_ref: Table 1 ETTh1 PatchTST+PIR; main_table/final_1 mean MSE 0.4373302161693573, manifest 0.43733
baseline.timing_scope: legacy protocol estimates retained for operational budgeting; not a measured v2 reference

leakage_remediation.verification_scope: Five-window four-horizon protocol smoke plus one original H96 checkpoint/model forward in a compatible runtime; no training or full evaluation.

allowed_changes: The revision architecture, retrieval/weighting method, quality estimator, revision training surrogate, optimizer and hyperparameters may change. The revision may be replaced completely while still operating on the fixed backbone forecasts and permitted context.

A pass must come from a change to the revision method: changing only existing constants or switches of the baseline revision (`--retrieval_num`, `--refine_lr`, `--refine_epochs`, `--refine_d_model`, `--refine_d_ff`, `--refine_layers`, `--including_time_features`, `--patience`) does not count (patch audit).
fixed_contract: Improve post-hoc revision of the fixed authors-trained PatchTST forecasts for the four ETTh1 horizons.
The PatchTST architecture and authors pretraining recipe are fixed; the selected pretrained parameters and normalization buffers must remain unchanged during revision.
The 96-step inputs, four horizons, original observations/splits/windows, float32 training standardization and equal-horizon mean MSE remain fixed.
Revision retrieval history contains training-split observations/targets only.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
method_freedom_review.budget_policy: agent overall deadline; separate overall formal replay budget
forbidden_substitutions: Do not substitute or fine-tune another backbone, change pretraining settings/initialization selection, update backbone buffers during revision, use validation/test history for retrieval, replace forecasting targets or change the metric.
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.

Revision models must take the fixed backbone forecast as an input and may not include a trainable copy of PatchTST, another model from `code/models`, or additional PatchTST seeds; those count as substituting or fine-tuning a backbone (patch audit).
For horizon H, only the fixed backbone trained for H supplies the backbone forecast; forecasts of the other horizons' backbones may not be blended in (patch audit).

evidence.finding: The curated score rule explicitly requires authors-trained PatchTST left unchanged and training-only revision history.

The paper studies a model-agnostic post-forecasting revision plugin and pretrained-backbone ablations. It does not itself establish a frozen-weights rule; that stricter rule is from the curated benchmark.
The old adaptation optimized all model parameters and updated BN buffers during revision, contradicting the curated guard. The corrected optimizer and revision mode freeze the backbone.

research_contract_review.verification_scope: Task-specific research-scope review and bounded checks; not a new performance/readiness certification.

validation_policy.learned_preprocessing: fit on training only; apply frozen fitted transforms to validation/test
validation_policy.instance_roles: Preserve explicit per-instance observation/training/calibration/causal-feedback roles; no evaluation-target fitting or validation-derived fitted state carried across independent cases.
validation_policy.enforcement: binding prompt and task contract; task-specific replay/guards where available; arbitrary training-data provenance requires source/patch audit
